title: Design Patterns
description: JavaScript and Angular design patterns, SOLID principles, dependency injection, trade-offs and simple practical implementations.

categories.title: Pattern Foundations
categories.description: What patterns are, when they help, and when they add unnecessary indirection.

topics.title: Design Patterns: What, Why and When
topics.description: A design pattern is a reusable way of organizing collaborating functions or objects for a recurring design problem; it is a decision template, not copy-paste code.

topics.title: Pattern vs Principle vs Architecture
topics.description: A principle guides judgment, a design pattern structures a local collaboration, and architecture defines system-wide boundaries, deployment and ownership.

topics.title: Coupling, Cohesion and Change
topics.description: Coupling is the dependency between units, while cohesion is how strongly the responsibilities inside one unit belong together.

topics.title: Composition Over Inheritance
topics.description: Composition builds behavior by combining small collaborators, while inheritance reuses behavior through an is-a hierarchy.

topics.title: Choosing Patterns Without Overengineering
topics.description: A pattern is justified by a concrete force such as multiple implementations, volatile policy, lifecycle complexity or cross-cutting behavior.

categories.title: SOLID Principles
categories.description: The five SOLID principles used as practical review questions, not just definitions.

topics.title: SOLID Principles Overview
topics.description: SOLID combines Single Responsibility, Open Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation and Dependency Inversion as tools for managing change.

topics.title: Single Responsibility Principle
topics.description: SRP means one cohesive responsibility or one primary reason to change, not literally one method per class.

topics.title: Open Closed Principle
topics.description: OCP means stable workflow code supports new behavior through controlled extension points instead of repeated edits.

topics.title: Liskov Substitution Principle
topics.description: LSP means every implementation can safely replace the contract it claims to implement without surprising the caller.

topics.title: Interface Segregation Principle
topics.description: ISP means consumers depend only on the capabilities they actually use.

topics.title: Dependency Inversion Principle
topics.description: DIP says high-level policy should depend on stable abstractions rather than concrete infrastructure such as HttpClient, localStorage or a vendor SDK.

categories.title: Creational Patterns
categories.description: Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Singleton and Prototype for controlled object creation.

topics.title: Factory Method Pattern
topics.description: Factory Method centralizes creation and returns a common contract while hiding which concrete implementation was selected.

topics.title: Abstract Factory Pattern
topics.description: Abstract Factory creates a compatible family of related collaborators without exposing their concrete classes.

topics.title: Builder Pattern
topics.description: Builder constructs a complex value through named steps and validates it before returning the final result.

topics.title: Singleton Pattern
topics.description: Singleton represents one instance for a defined scope, but the scope may be an app, route, component subtree, worker or server request.

topics.title: Prototype Pattern
topics.description: Prototype creates new configured values by cloning an existing example instead of rebuilding every property.

categories.title: Structural Patterns
categories.description: Adapter, Facade, Decorator, Proxy and Composite for composing and simplifying object relationships.

topics.title: Adapter Pattern
topics.description: Adapter converts an external or incompatible interface into the contract the application wants to consume.

topics.title: Facade Pattern
topics.description: Facade exposes a small cohesive use-case API over a more complicated group of services.

topics.title: Decorator Pattern
topics.description: Decorator wraps an object through the same contract and adds behavior before or after delegating to the original.

topics.title: Proxy Pattern
topics.description: Proxy stands in place of a target and controls access through caching, validation, lazy creation, measurement or restrictions.

topics.title: Composite Pattern
topics.description: Composite gives leaf items and groups a useful common contract so tree structures can be processed recursively.

categories.title: Behavioral Patterns
categories.description: Strategy, Observer, Command, State and other patterns for coordinating behavior and communication.

topics.title: Strategy Pattern
topics.description: Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind one behavior contract.

topics.title: Observer Pattern
topics.description: Observer creates a one-to-many relationship in which dependent observers react when a subject emits or changes.

topics.title: Publish Subscribe Pattern
topics.description: Publish Subscribe routes events through a broker so publishers and subscribers do not reference one another directly.

topics.title: Command Pattern
topics.description: Command represents an action as a value that can be executed, queued, logged, retried or undone.

topics.title: State Pattern
topics.description: State represents meaningful lifecycle stages explicitly so behavior changes according to the current state.

topics.title: Chain of Responsibility Pattern
topics.description: Chain of Responsibility passes a request through ordered handlers that may inspect, transform, stop or forward it.

topics.title: Template Method Pattern
topics.description: Template Method defines a stable algorithm sequence in a base class while subclasses override selected steps.

topics.title: Mediator Pattern
topics.description: Mediator centralizes coordination among participants that would otherwise hold many peer-to-peer references.

topics.title: Null Object Pattern
topics.description: Null Object provides a safe no-op or neutral implementation when absence is valid behavior.

categories.title: JavaScript Patterns
categories.description: Modules, closures, mixins, composition, memoization and other everyday JavaScript idioms.

topics.title: ES Module Pattern
topics.description: ES modules provide lexical scope plus explicit imports and exports that define a public API.

topics.title: Closure Based Encapsulation
topics.description: A closure lets returned functions retain access to private variables from the scope where they were created.

topics.title: Mixin Pattern
topics.description: A mixin adds a focused reusable capability to otherwise unrelated types without claiming a deep is-a hierarchy.

topics.title: Function Composition and Pipeline
topics.description: Function composition connects focused transformations so the output of one step becomes the input of the next.

topics.title: Memoization Pattern
topics.description: Memoization caches a deterministic function result by input so repeated calls can reuse previous work.

topics.title: Event Delegation Pattern
topics.description: Event delegation handles similar descendant events through one stable ancestor listener using DOM bubbling.

topics.title: Repository and Data Mapper Pattern
topics.description: Repository exposes domain-oriented data operations while Data Mapper translates external records into application models.

categories.title: Patterns Used in Angular
categories.description: How dependency injection, facades, adapters, RxJS and Signals map to classic design patterns in Angular.

topics.title: Why Dependency Injection Is Used in Angular
topics.description: Dependency Injection means a class declares the capability it needs while Angular provider configuration decides which instance or implementation supplies it.

topics.title: Angular Hierarchical Injector and Provider Scope
topics.description: Angular resolves dependencies through hierarchical environment and element injectors, so provider location determines sharing and lifetime.

topics.title: Angular Provider Strategies and InjectionToken
topics.description: Angular providers connect a token to useClass, useValue, useExisting or useFactory creation and selection rules.

topics.title: Facade Pattern in Angular
topics.description: An Angular facade gives components a small feature-oriented API over repositories, state, permissions and asynchronous orchestration.

topics.title: Adapter Pattern at the Angular API Boundary
topics.description: An Angular adapter maps backend DTOs and transport codes into stable feature models.

topics.title: Strategy Pattern with Angular Dependency Injection
topics.description: Angular DI can select one implementation of a strategy contract for a route, tenant, product or component subtree.

topics.title: Observer Pattern with RxJS and Angular Signals
topics.description: Signals model current reactive state and derivation, while RxJS models asynchronous streams with time, cancellation, errors and completion.

topics.title: Chain of Responsibility with Angular HTTP Interceptors
topics.description: Angular HTTP interceptors form an ordered middleware chain around HttpClient requests and responses.

topics.title: Decorator Pattern with Angular Directives and Pipes
topics.description: Angular attribute directives can layer reusable host behavior and pipes can layer reusable template transformations.

topics.title: State Pattern with Angular Signals
topics.description: Signals can hold an explicit discriminated-union state so the feature has one valid status at a time.

topics.title: Command and Use Case Services in Angular
topics.description: A use-case service exposes a business action such as approveInvoice or submitOrder and coordinates its required collaborators.

topics.title: Smart and Presentational Component Pattern
topics.description: A smart component connects to feature state and services, while a presentational component receives view data and emits semantic user intent.

topics.title: Dynamic Component Factory and Plugin Registry in Angular
topics.description: Dynamic rendering is factory-like: a controlled registry selects a component type and Angular creates it with inputs and injector context.

title: AI Concepts
description: AI and LLM fundamentals explained in simple human language, including transformers, prompting, embeddings, vector search, RAG types, agents, evaluation, security and production design.

categories.title: AI & LLM Foundations
categories.description: Core vocabulary for how large language models are built, sized and run.

topics.title: What Is a Language Model
topics.description: A language model is a system trained to predict the next token in a sequence, and every higher-level LLM behavior is built on top of that single prediction task.

topics.title: Tokens and Tokenization
topics.description: Tokenization splits text into sub-word units before a model ever sees it, which is why token count, not word count, drives cost, latency and context limits.

topics.title: Context Window and Its Limits
topics.description: The context window is the fixed number of tokens a model can attend to at once, and everything that does not fit must be summarized, retrieved or dropped.

topics.title: Training vs Inference
topics.description: Training adjusts model weights over large datasets and heavy compute, while inference is the comparatively cheap, weight-frozen step of generating a response to one prompt.

topics.title: Model Scale and Capability
topics.description: Parameter count, training data and compute jointly determine capability, but bigger is not always better once latency, cost and task fit are considered.

categories.title: Transformer Architecture
categories.description: Attention, positional encoding and the architectural choices behind modern LLMs.

topics.title: Self-Attention Explained
topics.description: Self-attention lets every token look at every other token in the sequence and weigh how much each one matters for predicting the next token.

topics.title: Multi-Head Attention
topics.description: Multi-head attention runs several attention computations in parallel so the model can track different kinds of relationships, such as syntax and long-range reference, at once.

topics.title: Positional Encoding
topics.description: Because self-attention has no built-in sense of order, positional encoding injects position information into token representations so word order still matters.

topics.title: Encoder-Decoder vs Decoder-Only Models
topics.description: Encoder-decoder models separate understanding the input from generating output, while decoder-only models like GPT do both with a single autoregressive stack.

topics.title: Why Transformers Replaced RNNs
topics.description: Transformers process a whole sequence in parallel through attention instead of one token at a time, which fixed the vanishing-gradient and long-range-dependency problems that limited RNNs.

categories.title: Prompting & Prompt Engineering
categories.description: Practical techniques for controlling what a model does and how it responds.

topics.title: Zero-Shot vs Few-Shot Prompting
topics.description: Zero-shot prompting asks a model to perform a task from instructions alone, while few-shot prompting adds a handful of worked examples to steer format and reasoning.

topics.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
topics.description: Chain-of-thought prompting asks a model to reason in intermediate steps before answering, which measurably improves accuracy on multi-step problems.

topics.title: System vs User Prompts
topics.description: The system prompt sets durable behavior, role and constraints for the whole conversation, while user prompts carry the specific, per-turn request.

topics.title: Sampling: Temperature and Top-p
topics.description: Temperature and top-p control how much randomness is allowed when the model samples the next token, trading determinism for creativity.

topics.title: Structured Output and JSON Mode
topics.description: Structured output constrains a model's response to a schema, using either prompt-level instructions or a grammar-constrained decoding mode, so downstream code can parse it reliably.

categories.title: Embeddings & Vector Search
categories.description: Turning text into vectors and searching them efficiently at scale.

topics.title: What Are Embeddings
topics.description: An embedding is a dense numeric vector that represents the meaning of text so that semantically similar inputs end up close together in vector space.

topics.title: Similarity Metrics
topics.description: Cosine similarity, dot product and Euclidean distance each answer how close two vectors are slightly differently, and the embedding model you use usually dictates which one to pick.

topics.title: Vector Databases
topics.description: A vector database indexes embeddings for fast approximate nearest-neighbor search at scale, trading a little recall for the speed a linear scan cannot provide.

topics.title: Chunking Strategies
topics.description: Chunking splits source documents into retrievable pieces, and the size, overlap and boundary rules you choose directly control retrieval quality.

topics.title: Hybrid Search
topics.description: Hybrid search combines keyword (lexical) search with vector (semantic) search so exact terms like IDs and acronyms are not lost to purely semantic matching.

categories.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
categories.description: Grounding model answers in retrieved data, and the trade-offs between RAG architectures.

topics.title: What Is RAG and Why It Matters
topics.description: RAG grounds a model's answer in retrieved documents at request time, which reduces hallucination and lets an application answer from private or fast-changing data without retraining.

topics.title: The Naive RAG Pipeline
topics.description: A naive RAG pipeline chunks and embeds documents ahead of time, then at query time retrieves the top matches and stuffs them into the prompt before generation.

topics.title: Reranking and Retrieval Quality
topics.description: A reranker re-scores the initial retrieved candidates with a more accurate but slower model, fixing the common case where the right chunk is retrieved but ranked too low to matter.

topics.title: Agentic RAG and Graph RAG
topics.description: Agentic RAG lets the model decide when and what to retrieve across multiple steps, while graph RAG retrieves through explicit entity relationships instead of flat chunk similarity.

topics.title: Evaluating RAG Quality
topics.description: RAG evaluation has to separately measure retrieval quality and generation quality, because good retrieval with a bad answer looks identical to bad retrieval from the outside.

categories.title: AI Agents & Tool Use
categories.description: Giving models the ability to act: tool calling, planning loops and multi-agent coordination.

topics.title: What Is an AI Agent
topics.description: An AI agent is a model wrapped in a loop that can choose actions, call tools and observe results across multiple steps instead of answering in a single pass.

topics.title: The ReAct Pattern
topics.description: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces with tool actions and their observations, letting the model adjust its plan based on what a tool actually returned.

topics.title: Function and Tool Calling
topics.description: Tool calling lets a model emit a structured request to invoke a named function with arguments, and the calling application executes it and returns the result for the model to continue with.

topics.title: Multi-Agent Systems
topics.description: Multi-agent systems split a task across specialized agents, such as a planner and several workers, which improves focus per agent but adds coordination and failure-handling overhead.

topics.title: Agent Memory and the Model Context Protocol
topics.description: Agent memory persists useful state across turns or sessions, and protocols like MCP standardize how an agent discovers and calls external tools and data sources.

categories.title: Fine-Tuning & Model Customization
categories.description: When to fine-tune instead of prompting or retrieving, and how modern fine-tuning actually works.

topics.title: Fine-Tuning vs Prompting vs RAG
topics.description: Prompting changes behavior instantly with no training, RAG adds fresh or private knowledge at query time, and fine-tuning bakes a skill or style into the weights themselves.

topics.title: LoRA and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
topics.description: LoRA and other PEFT methods train a small number of additional low-rank parameters instead of the whole model, making customization far cheaper and easier to swap per use case.

topics.title: RLHF and Alignment
topics.description: Reinforcement learning from human feedback trains a model to prefer the responses humans rate as better, which is how raw next-token predictors become helpful, instruction-following assistants.

topics.title: Distillation and Smaller Models
topics.description: Distillation trains a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model's outputs, recovering much of the capability at a fraction of the inference cost.

topics.title: Choosing a Model for a Task
topics.description: Model choice is a trade-off between capability, latency, cost and data sensitivity, and the right answer is often a smaller model plus good context rather than the largest model available.

categories.title: Evaluating AI Systems
categories.description: Measuring whether an LLM feature actually works, and catching regressions before users do.

topics.title: Evaluating LLM Outputs
topics.description: Evaluating an LLM feature means defining task-specific success criteria upfront, because generic fluency says nothing about whether the answer was actually correct or useful.

topics.title: LLM-as-Judge
topics.description: Using one model to grade another model's outputs against a rubric scales evaluation cheaply, but the judge itself needs calibration against human ratings to be trusted.

topics.title: Hallucination Detection
topics.description: A hallucination is a fluent, confident statement that is not supported by the model's training data or provided context, and catching it requires checking claims against a source, not just checking that the text sounds right.

topics.title: Golden Datasets and Regression Testing
topics.description: A golden dataset is a curated, versioned set of inputs with known-good outputs that lets you detect when a prompt, model or pipeline change silently breaks something that used to work.

topics.title: Benchmarks and Their Limits
topics.description: Public benchmarks are useful for comparing raw model capability, but they rarely resemble your actual task closely enough to substitute for evaluation on your own data.

categories.title: AI Security & Safety
categories.description: Prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage and the guardrails production AI systems need.

topics.title: Prompt Injection
topics.description: Prompt injection is untrusted content, such as a document or webpage, that tries to override a model's instructions, and it has to be treated as an attacker-controlled input, not just noisy data.

topics.title: Jailbreaks and Guardrails
topics.description: A jailbreak is a crafted input designed to bypass a model's safety training, and guardrails are the layered checks, filters and policies that catch what the model's own training misses.

topics.title: Data Leakage and PII
topics.description: Sensitive data can leak through prompts sent to a third-party model, through retrieved context surfaced to the wrong user, or through logs, so PII handling has to be designed at every stage of the pipeline.

topics.title: Content Moderation
topics.description: Content moderation screens both user input and model output for disallowed content, and doing it on both sides matters because a safe prompt can still produce an unsafe response.

topics.title: Sandboxing Tool Execution
topics.description: Because an agent's tool calls are ultimately driven by model output, every tool needs the same isolation, permission scoping and validation you would apply to any other untrusted caller.

categories.title: Production AI System Design
categories.description: Latency, cost, caching, streaming, observability and routing for real-world AI systems.

topics.title: Latency and Cost Trade-offs
topics.description: Every LLM feature trades off latency, cost and quality against model size, context length and number of calls, and production systems have to make that trade-off explicit rather than defaulting to the biggest model.

topics.title: Caching LLM Responses
topics.description: Caching identical or near-identical prompts avoids paying for and waiting on repeated generation, but it requires care around personalization, freshness and prompt-key design.

topics.title: Streaming Responses
topics.description: Streaming tokens back to the client as they are generated cuts perceived latency dramatically even when total generation time is unchanged, which is why almost every production chat UI streams.

topics.title: Observability and Tracing for LLM Pipelines
topics.description: LLM observability traces every prompt, retrieval, tool call and response in a request so you can debug a bad answer instead of only seeing the final text.

topics.title: Model Routing and Fallback
topics.description: Model routing sends each request to the cheapest model that can handle it and falls back to a stronger model or a cached/default response when a call fails or a provider is down.
